target:
abbrev Def1 := Set ArithmeticSentence
def Def5 (K : Def1) (F : ArithmeticTheory) : Prop := K = F.theory
def Def6 (K : Def1) : Prop := ∃ F : ArithmeticTheory, F.RE ∧ K ⊆ F.theory
a_raw: {"translation":"Def1 is an abbreviation for the type of sets of closed arithmetic sentences; no closure condition is imposed. For any such set K and any arithmetic theory F, Def5(K, F) means that K is exactly the set of theorems of F: for every arithmetic sentence σ, σ belongs to K if and only if F proves σ. Def5 does not require F to be recursively enumerable. For any set K of arithmetic sentences, Def6(K) means that there exists an arithmetic theory F whose axiom set is recursively enumerable and such that, for every sentence σ in K, F proves σ. The same F must work for all of K, but it may prove sentences outside K. Def6 does not require K itself to be recursively enumerable, its members to be axioms of F, or F to be consistent or sound."}
translation: Def1 is an abbreviation for the type of sets of closed arithmetic sentences; no closure condition is imposed. For any such set K and any arithmetic theory F, Def5(K, F) means that K is exactly the set of theorems of F: for every arithmetic sentence σ, σ belongs to K if and only if F proves σ. Def5 does not require F to be recursively enumerable. For any set K of arithmetic sentences, Def6(K) means that there exists an arithmetic theory F whose axiom set is recursively enumerable and such that, for every sentence σ in K, F proves σ. The same F must work for all of K, but it may prove sentences outside K. Def6 does not require K itself to be recursively enumerable, its members to be axioms of F, or F to be consistent or sound.

divergences.description: Def6 uses `K ⊆ F.theory` instead of `K = F.theory`. It requires the machine to produce every sentence in K but allows outputs outside K, contrary to Koellner’s requirement that the outputs coincide. In fact, the recursively enumerable theory with sole axiom ⊥ proves every sentence, so Def6 holds for every K.

judgement.summary: Def1 represents K as a set of arithmetic sentences, and Def5 expresses exact theorem-set equality with effectiveness left separate as stipulated. To express WMT, Def6 should be `∃ F : ArithmeticTheory, F.RE ∧ K = F.theory`.
